sb_prompt: DISCUSS HOW YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER KEEP UP ON CURRENT EVENTS.      DO YOU GET MOST OF YOUR NEWS FROM TVOR PEOPLE YOU KNOW?  ARE YOU SATISFIED WITH THE QUALITY OF COVERAGE?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hey, how's it going?
ParticipantA: Pretty good, just working on a transmission right now. You?
ParticipantB: Good, just getting some taxes done. So, how are you keeping up with the news these days?
ParticipantA: Honestly, it's all over the place. Mostly from people I know. My buddy Dave, he's in the same boat as me, sort of.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? What's he say about what's happening?
ParticipantA: Well, he says one thing and I say another. Some of it feels right, some of it... well, it just doesn't sit right with me.
ParticipantB: That's interesting. I've been thinking about this stuff for years. I think I made up my mind a long time ago.
ParticipantA: Oh? And what did you decide?
ParticipantB: I think the big stories are mostly real, but the way they're packaged... yeah, that's the thing. I just don't like the angle sometimes.
ParticipantA: See, that's exactly where Dave and I disagree. He thinks the angle is fine, I think it's a little skewed.
ParticipantB: Hmm. Well, I guess we're just different. I've got my head set on it, but I can't really explain why.
ParticipantA: Yeah, that happens. Sometimes you just feel it, even if you can't put it in words.
ParticipantB: Right. So, do you think the coverage is good overall, or just the parts you like?
ParticipantA: Mixed bag, I guess. The facts are there, but the spin is heavy. Like my friend's experience, it shapes how you see it.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I get that. Sometimes the details matter more than the headline.
ParticipantA: True. Well, at least we're talking about it. Most people just scroll past.
ParticipantB: Exactly. Thanks for chatting about this.
ParticipantA: Yeah, you too. Take care.
ParticipantB: You too, bye.
ParticipantA: Bye.
